blind_target.evidence_quote: Jones and Westoff (1979) reported a study of fertility trends among white women in intact first marriages.
blind_target.outcome_quote: We found that the fertility of the two religious groups was indeed converging, but the Catholic-non-Catholic differential was larger than that found by Jones and Westoff --how much larger depends on what measure is used. Moreover, we found that the differential by frequency of communion among Catholic wives was not converging.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract reports agreement on fertility convergence between religious groups but disagreement on convergence by communion frequency.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract identifies Jones and Westoff (1979) as the original study of fertility trends among white women in intact first marriages, then states that this paper replicated their study and compares the same Catholic/non-Catholic fertility-convergence finding. Supplied row 2255 identifies that same work as Westoff and Jones (1979), titled ‘The end of “Catholic” fertility’; the reversed author order and absent title in the abstract do not indicate a distinct study.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Jones and Westoff (1979) reported a study of fertility trends among white women in intact first marriages. They found that the fertility of white Catholic and non-Catholic wives was converging.
luna_triage.duplicate_quote: We replicated their study using data from the 1976 National Survey of Family Growth. We found that the fertility of the two religious groups was indeed converging
